text:
Priya Shah: quick question for the group — when the edge gateway transparently routes a request to a fallback execution pool (e.g. quantized-2 or pooled-fallback) due to capacity/latency policies, what should the console/billing show as the cost/quota owner? tenants are seeing token spikes in their dashboards and support tickets are increasing.
Alex Kim: current behavior is simple: runtime tags the trace but billing attributes tokens to whoever executed the request. so if exec_account is pixel-pool-7 it bills the pool. that gives infra a clean chargeback but confusing tenant UX.
Mateo Rivera: we implemented that originally to keep infra accounting simple. downside: product teams with strict quotas get false 429s or unexpected quota usage.
Sophie Li: from a UX standpoint we need one canonical "owner" for tenant-facing views (quota, alerts). Having billing attribution differ from quota owner is allowed, but default console view should be stable for tenants.
Priya Shah: proposal: logical ownership vs execution billing. Logical owner = the tenant who initiated request (used for quotas and tenant alerts). Execution billing = infra account that actually consumed resources (used for finance/chargeback). Both recorded in telemetry.
Alex Kim: doable. Implementation sketch: gateway injects X-Logical-Owner and X-Route-Decision into the proxied request. runtime emits two independent meters: tenant_meter(tenant_id, tokens) and exec_meter(exec_account, tokens). Traces include route.decide and route.exec_account so we can join later.
Mateo Rivera: important: quota enforcement must have a realtime signal. Gateway should try to acquire a token-lease from quota-service before routing large token requests. Otherwise we risk race conditions where multiple gateways overcommit and runtime rejects or routes to fallback.
Sophie Li: UX needs: default panel shows tenant-centric usage (logical owner). Add an "Execution breakdown" accordion showing which variant/executor served tokens and infra account. Also surface a clear label when a fallback happened (e.g., "served by fallback variant due to capacity").
Jordan (prodeng): for post-incident analysis we need structured route events: {trace_id, logical_owner, exec_account, variant, policy, reason}. That lets billing and SREs reconcile costs with tenant complaints.
Alex Kim: small wrinkle: some fallbacks change semantics (e.g., shorter context window). If we preserve logical ownership for quota but result differs, that could be a surprise for customers. We should record route_reason and a brief capability-diff tag.
Priya Shah: agreed. UX / contract rules: 1) quota checks and alerts use logical owner; 2) billing uses exec_account; 3) console shows both but tenant view prioritized; 4) flag any semantic downgrade next to the request in traces.
Mateo Rivera: operational concern: metrics cardinality if we start emitting exec_account + tenant + variant dimensions. Suggest sampling route events at low rate (1%) by default, and emit full detail for errors and canary traffic. Aggregate meters (tenant_meter and exec_meter) should be low-cardinality (just tenant_id or exec_account).
Alex Kim: also consider a lightweight lease RPC pattern: gateway calls quota-service.acquire(tenant_id, tokens) -> returns lease_id or fail. If lease granted, attach lease_id to request headers so runtime can decrement the same lease instead of rechecking. If runtime serves via fallback and exec_account != primary, runtime still emits exec_meter but tenant_meter reconciles via lease_id.
Priya Shah: that would keep tenant quotas consistent across gateways and reduce false 429s. What about rollout UX when we flip models (canary -> rollout)? Customers should be able to opt into seeing variant-level token breakdowns or keep default aggregated view.
Sophie Li: propose two console toggles: "Show execution chargeback (finance)" and "Reveal variant-level breakdown". Defaults: both OFF for tenant dashboards, ON for internal/finance views. We should also add an annotation in recent-activity if any request used a fallback variant.
Jordan (prodeng): billing side asks for a join key. Use trace_id and request_id in both tenant and exec meters. We'll also need a stable exec_account naming scheme (e.g., infra:pool/region/type). I'll coordinate with billing to confirm they can ingest exec_meter lines.
Alex Kim: rollout plan: prototype header propagation and lease RPC in the gateway shim; instrument runtime to emit both meters and route events. Start with sampling enabled (1% detailed traces) and full count meters only for tenant_id and exec_account. deploy-bot: gateway-canary deployed -> id gateway-canary-2026-03-21-a
Priya Shah: I'll write a short RFC with: header contract (X-Logical-Owner, X-Route-Decision, X-Route-Reason, X-Lease-ID), meter semantics (tenant_meter vs exec_meter), lease RPC sketch, trace attributes, and console UX toggles & mockups. Can we review tomorrow morning?
Mateo Rivera: I'll fill in the quota lease API and edge cases (lease expiry, partial token grants).
Sophie Li: I'll mock the execution details accordion and the default tenant view.
Alex Kim: I'll add a debug endpoint on the shim to replay route events for customer support.
Jordan (prodeng): I'll engage billing and finance to confirm exec_meter consumption.
Priya Shah: thanks — tagging follow-ups: @Alex Kim please include capability-diff enums; @Jordan (prodeng) confirm finance ingestion. :thumbsup:
